data.narrative:
Caelux is a Series A climate and energy company that has raised $75M to date. The comparable universe consists of nine same-sector peers: one public company (LNZA) and eight private firms including Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen.

Stage-progression analysis is the applicable valuation method. Using total capital raised of $75M as a proxy for post-money value at the most recent round, a typical 2.0x step-up multiplier from Series A to the subsequent stage yields an implied valuation of $150M. This methodology rests on observed progression patterns across similar-stage companies and does not rely on transaction multiples or revenue metrics.

Peer-median analysis is not applicable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables within the Climate & Energy sector. Although nine peers exist in the sector, none of the narrow filters—same stage, adjacent stage, or similar valuation tier—returned three or more data points necessary for robust triangulation. A broad sector median would risk introducing material bias given the stage and capital heterogeneity within climate tech.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $128M (low) to $172M (high), with a median of $150M. This single-method triangulation carries elevated uncertainty. Key risks to valuation include the absence of revenue traction or technology milestones in the data provided, which limits validation of stage-appropriate progression multiples. Resolution of these gaps would strengthen the analysis.
